question.text: This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).
question.clue: Its southern boundary is formed by the Pindus Mountains and its longest river is the Drin, which empties in the north.

swap.leadin: Its source is in the Black Forest region of Germany.
swap.text: Name this river that flows through Vienna long before it reaches the Black Sea.
swap.clue: Despite not being native to it, the Phanariotes served as administrators of a region on this river.

question.text: This former Yugoslav President was tried for war crimes at The Hague, but died in prison in of a heart attack in 2006 while still awaiting a verdict.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
swap.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
swap.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

question.leadin: His most famous action led to the July Crisis.
question.text: Name this Serbian assassin who fatally shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand and thus helped cause World War I.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.leadin: The destroyed Vukovar Water Tower was preserved to commemorate massacres against this country's people.
swap.text: Name this country which was led in its war of independence by Franjo Tudjman. Separatists in this country led the Log Revolution and bombarded the medieval Old Town of Dubrovnik.
swap.clue: Separatists in this modern-day country blockaded roads using trees in the so-called "Log Revolution."

question.leadin: In this leader's last public appearance, people shouted "Timisoara" in reference to an uprising he had violently suppressed.
question.text: Name this long-time Communist leader of Romania. This man and his wife's execution was nearly caught on live television following a 1989 revolution.
question.clue: In an effort to increase his country's population, he outlawed almost all forms ofcontraception in Decree 770, and he employed a secret police known as the Securitate.

swap.text: Much of the ethnic strife of the 90s dates back to the atrocities of this Croatian ultranationalist organization formed by Ante Pavelic that cooperated with the Nazis in WWII.
swap.clue: This group of terrorists whose slogan "Za dom Spremni" means "Ready for the Fatherland."

question.leadin: The early rulers of these people, including Asparukh, are listed in the Nominalia.
question.text: Name these people who were soundly defeated at the Battle of Kleidion by Basil II, who was nicknamed the "Slayer" of these people.
question.clue: The Paulicians may have inspired a Gnostic, dualistic sect which arose among these people called Bogomilism.

swap.leadin: A leader of these people left an army and used a forged letter to take over Kruje ("CREW-huh").
swap.text: Name these people who unified in the League of Lezhe ("leh-ZHUH"). The Treaty of Gaeta ended a revolt of these people led by the folk hero Skanderbeg.
swap.clue: People of this ethnicity were the target of the Racak Massacre, whose perpetrators claimed to be targeting a paramilitary group led by Hashim Thaci .

question.text: Kostunica was president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia until March 2003, one month after the country adopted this new name. The country would keep this name until its two constituents broke apart in June 2006.

swap.leadin: This event was called "the darkest page in my life" by the Russian representative.
swap.text: Name this 1878 meeting that hashed out the state of the Balkans following the Russo-Turkish War. It produced a treaty that replaced the Treaty of San Stefano.
swap.clue: Another key participant here was Gyula Andrassy, who negotiated the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary.

question.leadin: Besides Germany, this country contributed the most troops to the fascist invasion of the USSR.
question.text: Name this country, which lost Bessarabia and North Bukovina in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and then regained those territories in Operation Barbarossa. This country's Conducator overthrew its king Carol II.
question.clue: Though briefly restored by King Michael's Coup, this country's monarchy was abolished and replaced by the Iron Guard in 1940.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the hit Serbian propaganda song "God is a Serb," sometimes erroneously called "Serbia Strong."
swap.text: "God is a Serb" refers to Croats as members of this fascist organization. Founded by Ante Pavelic, it collaborated with German and Italian occupiers and nominally ruled Croatia during World War II.
swap.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

question.leadin: This country's war of independence began a year after the Log Revolution and included the Vukovar massacre.
question.text: Name this country that carried out Operation Storm, resulting in the defeat of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.
question.clue: A water tower riddled with bullets in this country's independence war was preserved in Vukovar.

swap.leadin: This politician launched Operation Storm, the armed takeover of the Republic of Serbian Krajina ("KRAH-ee-nah"), after it refused to adopt the Z-4 Plan for reintegration with Croatia.
swap.text: Name this president of Croatia throughout most of the 1990s. He signed the Erdut Agreement with the remaining independent republics and thus fully achieved Croatian independence.
swap.clue: Along with Milosevic, this neofascist Croatian dictator was party to the earlier 1995 Dayton Accords, which allowed for the NATO implementation force to take over for U.N. peacekeepers in Bosnia.

question.leadin: Jason Vuic profiled Malcolm Bricklin's import of this product to America after five-hundred some alterations to reach US standards in a book about "The Rise and Fall" of this product.
question.text: Give this brand name of notoriously shoddy imports that were sold in their homeland as Korals. This product's production was crippled by a 1999 NATO bombing of a facility mistaken for Zastava's arms factory.
question.answerHtml: Yugos [or the Zastava Yugo; or the Yugo Koral; accept the Yugo GV; accept The Yugo: The Rise and Fall of the Worst Car in History]

swap.leadin: The principle signatory of this treaty was forbidden from having an army larger than 20,000 men, and was forced to pay 100 million pounds in reparations.
swap.text: Name this 1919 treaty, which forced a certain Central Power to renounce their claim to Western Thrace.
swap.answerHtml: Treaty of Neuilly-sur-Seine [when reading the answer to a team that didn’t get it, leave off “sur Seine”]

question.text: Tuđman launched Operation Storm and obliterated the forces of Serbian Krajina after agreeing to lend this leader military aid via the Split Agreement. With Tuđman and Slobodon Milosevic, this first President of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed the 1995 Dayton Accords.

swap.text: Unfortunately for Murad, he was assassinated by this Serbian national hero toward the end of that very same Battle of Kosovo.
swap.clue: According to tradition, this was the name of the Serbian soldier that assassinated the sultan Murad. He is venerated as a saint in the Serbian church and is celebrated in the epic poem The Mountain Wreath.
